claims.text: Platforms produce and allocate visibility rather than merely distorting a neutral flow of communication.
Visibility is defined as the institutionally produced probability that a communicative act will be delivered to an audience.
The Algorithmic Empowerment Principle (AEP) articulates platforms' epistemic responsibilities as gatekeepers of public attention.
The Algorithmic Empowerment Principle holds that platforms with gatekeeping power owe structurally disadvantaged groups a fair opportunity for epistemic participation.
When background inequality measurably reduces a group's fair chance to reach an audience, platforms should allocate a reasonable additional share of algorithmic attention to its speech.
Duties of epistemic redress govern platform ranking design.
Duties of epistemic redress include visibility audits.
Duties of epistemic redress require platforms to justify their choices to affected communities.

methodologies.name: Algorithmic Empowerment Principle (AEP)
methodologies.description: A normative framework based on epistemic injustice scholarship delineating platforms' epistemic duties to allocate additional visibility to structurally disadvantaged groups.

limitations.text: Much algorithmic fairness scholarship relies on the language of noninterference, evaluating platforms primarily by whether they distort an assumed neutral flow of communication.
